LESSON: MATCHING AND PAIRING

Grade: PP1
Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES
Strand: CLASSIFICATION
Topic 1.2: Matching and Pairing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Matching and Pairing. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Which objects look and Pairing learner should be able to: similar different objects from the alike?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify differences among and pairing objects according to 3.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Today’s maths focus is Matching and Pairing.

• Start with objects you can touch or draw — stones, sticks, bottle tops, or drawings in your book.

• Say the steps aloud as you work so you do not skip a stage.

• Check your answer with a second method or by estimating.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market, count 10 mangoes and put them in 2 groups of 5.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row and write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and receive 5 more, you have 12 shillings.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Solve three short problems about Matching and Pairing using drawings.
2. Explain one solution to a partner in your own words.
3. Make up one new word problem set in your county or school.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five practice questions and solve them in your book.
2. Show your working clearly — not only the final answer.
3. Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson with bottle tops or drawings.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. In groups or in pairs, individual learners match and pair objects according to likeness, sameness or use
2. Learners relate objects to their use in the environment.
3. Learners sing songs or recite poems on relationship or use of objects from the environment.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which objects look and Pairing learner should be able to: similar different objects from the alike?
2. What makes them look 8 lessons objects in the environment • Teacher demonstrates matching alike?
3. How do we use these objects in the environment one attribute (sameness, likeness objects?
4. How can we care for environment • Few learners demonstrate these objects?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Use objects or drawings when a sum feels hard.
2. Check every answer.
3. Matching and Pairing is used in real Kenyan life — market, school, and home.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.
